subject.title: [Bug]: browser navigation-guard explicit hostname allowlist broken by SSRF loopback tightening (#100835)

question: Should browser navigation exact-host or pattern allowlist entries continue to permit non-localhost hostnames that resolve to loopback after the trusted-host SSRF hardening?
rationale: Both directions change a security-sensitive contract: preserving the old test restores operator-declared browser exceptions, while retiring it keeps the accepted SSRF protection against non-localhost loopback rebinding.

options.title: Retire the old loopback-alias contract
options.body: Keep the merged SSRF hardening and update browser navigation tests/docs to require explicit localhost, loopback literals, or deliberate private-network opt-in for loopback access.

options.title: Approve a scoped browser exception
options.body: Allow only the maintainer-approved loopback case while preserving metadata/link-local DNS-answer rejection and adding focused tests plus real browser proof.

options.title: Defer to broader SSRF design
options.body: Keep this issue and the linked PR blocked until the browser SSRF allowlist model is decided together with adjacent private-network policy work.

recommendation.title: Retire the old loopback-alias contract
recommendation.body: Keep the merged SSRF hardening and update browser navigation tests/docs to require explicit localhost, loopback literals, or deliberate private-network opt-in for loopback access.

likelyOwner.reason: They opened the current issue and have the strongest recent browser/SSRF boundary history in the inspected commits and linked PR discussions.
